title: 93. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Simplifying Ratios
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Reduce a two-term ratio to coprime integer terms.
questions.question: Simplify \(14:21\).
questions.explanation: The greatest common divisor is \(7\). Dividing both terms by \(7\) gives \(2:3\). The alternative divides the terms by different factors.
questions.hint: Use the same common divisor for both terms.

questions.concept: Reducing a Ratio of Multiples of Five
questions.learningObjective: Reduce a two-term integer ratio using the greatest common divisor.
questions.question: Simplify \(25:10\).
questions.explanation: Divide both terms by their greatest common divisor \(5\) to get \(5:2\). The alternative divides the second term by \(10\) instead of \(5\).
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor of the two terms.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize whether ratio terms have a common factor.
questions.question: Which ratio is already in simplest form?
questions.explanation: The terms \(8\) and \(15\) have greatest common divisor \(1\), so they cannot be reduced. The terms \(9\) and \(15\) share factor \(3\), giving \(3:5\).
questions.hint: Check whether the two terms share a positive divisor greater than one.

questions.learningObjective: Reduce every term of a three-part ratio by the same common divisor.
questions.question: Simplify \(18:30:42\).
questions.explanation: The greatest common divisor of all three terms is \(6\). Dividing each term by \(6\) gives \(3:5:7\). The alternative changes the last proportion.
questions.hint: Use a divisor common to all three terms.

questions.learningObjective: Convert decimal ratio terms to integers before reducing.
questions.question: Simplify \(0.45:0.75\) to coprime positive integer terms.
questions.explanation: Multiplying both terms by \(100\) gives \(45:75\). Dividing both by \(15\) gives \(3:5\). The alternative does not preserve the quotient of the original terms.
questions.hint: Clear decimal places by scaling every term by the same power of ten.

questions.learningObjective: Clear fractional denominators with a common multiplier.
questions.question: Simplify \(\frac{2}{3}:\frac{5}{4}\) to coprime positive integer terms.
questions.explanation: Multiply both terms by the common denominator \(12\): \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\times12=8\) and \(\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)\times12=15\). Their greatest common divisor is one. The alternative multiplies numerators and denominators in the wrong positions.
questions.hint: Multiply every term by a common multiple of the denominators.

questions.concept: Simplifying a Ratio with Mixed Length Units
questions.learningObjective: Convert quantities to a common unit before reducing their ratio.
questions.question: Simplify the ratio \(1.2\text{ m}:45\text{ cm}\).
questions.explanation: Convert \(1.2\text{ m}=120\text{ cm}\). Then \(120:45\) divides by \(15\) to give \(8:3\). The alternative reduces \(1.2:45\) without converting units.
questions.hint: Express both lengths in the same unit before simplifying.

questions.learningObjective: Use a common denominator and then reduce all ratio terms.
questions.question: Simplify \(\frac{1}{2}:\frac{3}{4}:\frac{5}{8}\) to coprime positive integer terms.
questions.explanation: Multiply every term by \(8\) to obtain \(4:6:5\). The three integers have greatest common divisor one. The alternative drops denominators without applying a common multiplier.
questions.hint: Clear all denominators using one common multiplier.

questions.learningObjective: Detect unequal scaling in a proposed simplification.
questions.question: A student simplifies \(24:36\) to \(4:9\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The result is correct because each term was divided by one of its factors.

options.label: B
options.text: The result is incorrect because the terms were divided by different factors; the simplest ratio is \(2:3\).

questions.explanation: The first term was divided by \(6\), but the second by \(4\), which changes the ratio. Divide both original terms by \(12\) to get \(2:3\). Being a factor of a term is insufficient; both terms need the same scale factor.
questions.hint: Compare the scale factor applied to each term.

questions.learningObjective: Combine decimal scaling with a greatest common divisor.
questions.question: A mixture uses three ingredients in amounts \(0.36\), \(0.54\), and \(0.90\) litres. What is their ratio in coprime positive integer terms, in the given order?
questions.explanation: Multiply by \(100\) to obtain \(36:54:90\). The greatest common divisor is \(18\), and division by \(18\) gives \(2:3:5\). The alternative scales the last amount inconsistently.
questions.hint: Clear the decimals first, then find a divisor common to all three integer terms.
